topic: The gospel album Elvis insisted on making when no one thought it would sell
script: Sixty-six years ago today, Elvis Presley released an album with no rock and roll on it at all. He was less than eight months out of the Army when he walked into RCA Studio B in Nashville. It was late October, 1960. Beside him stood the Jordanaires. And he sang the church music he had carried since boyhood in Tupelo. The record was called His Hand in Mine. The whole album was cut in one session that ran about fourteen hours. One song from those sessions, Crying in the Chapel, was held back for more than four years. In 1965 it climbed to number three in America, and number one in Britain. The album itself kept selling, quietly, for decades. Gold in 1969. Platinum in 1992. And the man the world called the King of Rock and Roll won every one of his competitive Grammys singing gospel.

sources.claim: His Hand in Mine released November 23, 1960 by RCA Victor (66 years ago today); an all-gospel album
Recorded October 30-31, 1960 at RCA Studio B, Nashville; all selections completed in one ~14-hour session
Elvis discharged from the Army March 5, 1960 (under eight months before the session)
Elvis's first songs were gospel at church in Tupelo, and he never stopped singing them (Graceland, quoted)
Crying in the Chapel recorded at the October 1960 sessions, withheld, released April 1965
Crying in the Chapel reached #3 on the Billboard Hot 100
Crying in the Chapel reached #1 in the UK
His Hand in Mine certified RIAA Gold April 9, 1969 and Platinum March 27, 1992
All three of Elvis's competitive Grammys were for gospel/inspirational recordings (1968, 1973, 1975 ceremonies)
